newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down as talk of bank bailout is disproved.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down as talk of bank bailout is disproved.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended down on Thursday, after market speculation that the Bank of Japan would announce a bailout of a financial institution in the afternoon was later disproved.

"Speculation swirled in the market in the afternoon that the Bank of Japan might announce a bailout of a financial institution in the afternoon. JGBs began falling once the market realized such talk was false," said a trust bank trader.
The December contract remained stuck in positive territory for much of the afternoon, but began a downturn in the late afternoon.

"Market sentiment was strong when speculation that BOJ might announce a bailout of a financial institution circulated in the market. Those who used the talk as a reason to build long positions sold once the rumour turned out to be false," said a city bank trader.

Traders said the Tokyo Credit Association's announcement that it would unveil a rescue plan for Musashino Shinkin, a small local credit association, had little effect on JGBs. "The market already knew about that," said the first trader.
The December closed at the day's low of 121.23, down from Wednesday's 121.44.
The high for the day was 121.54.

Position adjustment ahead of the announcement of Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) data for the April-June quarter at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) on Friday may have also driven JGBs down toward the close, some traders said.
Various traders said the market was expecting an annualised drop of about four percent, on average.
Market sentiment was upbeat in the morning, supported by good demand from various investors and an outright bond buying operation by the Ministry of Finance.
"JGB futures were sold more than cash bonds today. It seemed like some people were involved in large-lot trade of JGB futures during the day," the second trader said.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB was yielding 2.925 percent as of 0709 GMT, up from Wednesday's 2.910 percent.
